chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad told me, saying: Ibn Muni'a told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shoyba narrated to us, from Sharik, from Al-Rakin, from Na'eem ibn Hanzale, from Ammar, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
He who has two faces in this world will have two tongues of fire on the Day of Resurrection.
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of being two-faced in Islam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Khisal*, this hadith emphasizes the spiritual consequence of *riya* (showing off) and *nifaq* (hypocrisy), where outward duality manifests as inner torment. The 'two tongues of fire' symbolize the dual nature of the hypocrite’s speech and judgment, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that inner sincerity must align with outward action. This warning serves as a practical guide for believers to maintain consistency between their public persona and private devotion.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-18 Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad narrated that Ibn Muni’a quoted on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shoyba’, on the authority of Abu Muawiyah, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Al-Rakin, on the authority of Na’eem ibn Hanzale’, on the authority of Am’mar that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “
The people who are two-faced in this world will have two tongues of Fire on the Resurrection Day.”
